title: Transform Array to All Equal Elements
summary: Given an array of integers consisting solely of 1 and -1, and an integer k, determine if it's possible to make all elements equal by performing at most k operations.
statement: Given an array of integers consisting solely of 1 and -1, and an integer k, determine if it's possible to make all elements equal by performing at most k operations. Each operation involves multiplying two adjacent elements by -1.
constraints: nums has up to 100,000 entries, each either one or negative one.
One operation flips the signs of two adjacent entries; the same pair may be chosen repeatedly.
Return whether either uniform target is reachable using at most k operations.
hints: Once a target sign is chosen, scanning left to right forces whether each adjacent pair must be flipped.
Greedily fix each position using its pair with the next position, then verify the last sign; test both targets.
Track whether the preceding pair flipped the current position; flip the next pair when the effective value differs, then verify the final value.
No later operation can change a position after its right-adjacent pair is passed, so every greedy choice is forced and therefore uses the unique minimum count for that target.
editorial: No later operation can change a position after its right-adjacent pair is passed, so every greedy choice is forced and therefore uses the unique minimum count for that target.

tests.explanation: Two adjacent-pair flips make every entry one, within the limit.
Neither all-one nor all-negative-one is reachable within the limit.
